title: Parametrized route do no ignore the trailing slash even if explicitely told to
description:
My understanding of `ignore_trailing_slash = TRUE` is that the route will be matched both by `/demo` & `/demo/`. 

This works as expected for standard path, but doesn't seem to work with parametrized path. 

Here is a reprex : 

```r
routes <- RouteStack$new()
one_route <- Route$new()
one_route$add_handler(
  'get',
  '/demo/:id',
  function(request, response, keys, ..., ignore_trailing_slash = TRUE) {
    cli::cat_rule('DEMO')
    print(keys)
    TRUE
  }
)
routes$add_route(one_route, 'one_route')

# Works
rook <- fiery::fake_request(
  'http://example.com/demo/colin',
  method = 'get'
)
req <- reqres::Request$new(rook)
routes$dispatch(req)
── DEMO ────────
$id
[1] "colin"

[1] TRUE

# I would have expected this to match as well
rook <- fiery::fake_request(
  'http://example.com/demo/colin/',
  method = 'get'
)
req <- reqres::Request$new(rook)
routes$dispatch(req)
[1] TRUE
attr(,"class")
[1] "routr_no_match"
```

title: FR: isolate the route dispatch to be able to return the value of the handler instead of TRUE/FALSE
How do I handle dispatch of routes if my app is not served at the root (`/`) of the server
description:
Let's say I'm serving an app at `'http://example.com/my-app/'` and I want to create routes that dispatch to `/` (so `'http://example.com/my-app/'` and another to `'http://example.com/my-app/demo/'`. 

So, this will work as long as I'm serving on `/`


```
routes <- RouteStack$new()

first <- Route$new()
first$add_handler(
  'get',
  '/',
  function(request, response, keys, ...) {
    cli::cat_rule('ALL')
    TRUE
  }
)
second <- Route$new()
second$add_handler(
  'get',
  '/demo/',
  function(request, response, keys, ...) {
    cli::cat_rule('DEMO')
    TRUE
  }
)
routes$add_route(first, 'first')
routes$add_route(second, 'second')

# Send a request through
rook <- fiery::fake_request(
  'http://example.com/demo/',
  method = 'get'
)
req <- reqres::Request$new(rook)
routes$dispatch(req)
── DEMO ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
[1] TRUE
```

But what if I want the dispatch to do 
- `"http://example.com/my-app/'` -> `first`
- `"http://example.com/my-app/demo/'` -> `second`

I tried working with the `root` param but it doesn't seem to work as expected 🤔 

In other word, how do I make this dispatch correctly?

```
rook <- fiery::fake_request(
  'http://example.com/my-app/.demo/',
  method = 'get'
)
req <- reqres::Request$new(rook)
routes$dispatch(req)
```

Thanks a lot

title: ressource_route: if default file used, content-type incorrect?
description:
if the default file is used (because the path ends in '/'), it appears that the file extension isn't set, and the file is returned, but with an incorrect 'content-type' (i assume it is):
````
bash % wget -v http://127.0.0.1:8080
--2020-11-09 20:22:48--  http://127.0.0.1:8080/
Connecting to 127.0.0.1:8080... connected.
HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 200 OK
Length: 1321 (1.3K) [text/plain]
Saving to: ‘index.html.2’

index.html.2                                    100%[======================================================================================================>]   1.29K  --.-KB/s    in 0s

2020-11-09 20:22:48 (136 MB/s) - ‘index.html.2’ saved [1321/1321]
````

this patch, which sets the default file earlier in the handler, seems to fix that.  (what it *breaks*, ...?)
````
diff --git a/R/ressource_route.R b/R/ressource_route.R
index 549d856..02021fe 100644
--- a/R/ressource_route.R
+++ b/R/ressource_route.R
@@ -109,13 +109,13 @@ ressource_route <- function(..., default_file = 'index.html', default_ext = 'htm
   assert_that(has_attr(mappings, 'names'))
   route$add_handler('get', '/*', function(request, response, keys, ...) {
     path <- request$path
+    if (grepl('/$', path)) path <- paste0(path, default_file)
     file_extension <- file_ext(path)
     has_ext <- file_extension != ''
     found <- FALSE
     file <- NA
     enc <- NA
     real_file <- NA
-    if (grepl('/$', path)) path <- paste0(path, default_file)
     for (i in seq_along(mappings)) {
       mount <- names(mappings)[i]
       if (!grepl(paste0('^', mount), path)) next
````

with this patch, here is how `wget` runs
````
bash % wget http://127.0.0.1:8080
--2020-11-09 20:39:15--  http://127.0.0.1:8080/
Connecting to 127.0.0.1:8080... connected.
HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 200 OK
Length: 1321 (1.3K) [text/html]
Saving to: ‘index.html.3’

index.html.3                                    100%[======================================================================================================>]   1.29K  --.-KB/s    in 0s

2020-11-09 20:39:15 (126 MB/s) - ‘index.html.3’ saved [1321/1321]
````

(this seems to make the browser launched by `fiery::Fire$ignite()`'s `showcase` work, at least for me.)

title: Add method to retrieve a route's handler
description:
### Motivation

It can be useful to overwrite a route's handler by first obtaining that handler, then writing a new handler which may call the old handler. For an example, [Dash does this](https://github.com/plotly/dash-auth/blob/7a412877f1d1690ca1ac28f6048927e6c4fc565f/dash_auth/auth.py#L16) to enable an authenticated "superclass" via flask's view_functions property

### Implementation

Looking at the [current `remove_handler()` method](https://github.com/thomasp85/routr/blob/f1687a492fdac8564b7fcf288e437f7f275e9370/R/route.R#L158-L167), perhaps we could add a method that essentially does this?

```r
get_handler = function (method, path) {
    id <- private$find_id(method, path)
    if (is.null(id)) {
        warning("No handler assigned to ", method, " and ", path, 
            call. = FALSE)
    }
  get(id, envir = private$handlerStore)
}
```


If this sounds useful, I'll take a stab at a PR

title: Relaying R (handler) errors to R console
description:
Looks as though (route handler) errors are relayed in the response to the client (in the body), but I could see use cases where you may also/rather want to relay that error to the R console (makes debugging easier, if nothing else)

```r
library(routr)
library(fiery)

route <- Route$new()
route$add_handler("get", "/", function(request, response, keys, ...) {
  message("Handler was triggered ")
  stop("Oops, something went wrong", call. = FALSE)
  TRUE
})

router <- RouteStack$new()
router$add_route(route, "name")

app <- Fire$new()
app$attach(router)
app$ignite(showcase = TRUE)
```
